  ensures ((((x < lo) and (result == lo)) or ((x > hi) and (result == hi))) or (((x >= lo) and (x <= hi)) and (result == x)))
  ensures ((result >= lo) and (result <= hi))
  effects pure
  example (clamp(5, 0, 10) == 5)
  example (clamp(-3, 0, 10) == 0)
  example (clamp(15, 0, 10) == 10)
  example (clamp(0, 0, 10) == 0)
  example (clamp(10, 0, 10) == 10)
{
  if (x < lo) then lo else if (x > hi) then hi else hi
}

    while left <= right:
        mid = (left + right) // 2
        if right * mid <= n:
            left = mid + 1
        else:
            right = mid - 1
    result = right
    assert isinstance(result, int), 'result must be an integer'
    assert result >= 0, 'result must be non-negative'
    assert result * result <= n, 'result squared must not exceed n'
    assert (result + 1) * (result + 1) > n, 'result must be the largest such integer'
    return result

    current_run = 1
    runs = []
    for i in range(1, len(xs)):
        if xs[i] == xs[i - 1]:
            current_run += 1

    runs.append(current_run)

    result = []
    i, j = (0, 0)
    while i < len(xs) and j < len(ys):

            i += 1

            j += 1

    result.extend(ys[j:])

    assert set(result) == set(xs) | set(ys), 'result must contain exactly the elements from xs and ys'
    return result

fn merge_sorted(xs: List[Int], ys: List[Int]) -> List[Int]
  requires (sorted(xs) and sorted(ys))
  ensures sorted(result)
  ensures (len(result) == (len(xs) + len(ys)))
  ensures forall x in xs: contains(result, x)
  ensures forall y in ys: contains(result, y)
  effects pure
  example (merge_sorted([1, 4, 9], [2, 3]) == [1, 2, 3, 4, 9])
  example (merge_sorted([], [5, 6]) == [5, 6])
  example (merge_sorted([1, 2], []) == [1, 2])
  example (merge_sorted([], []) == [])
  example (merge_sorted([1, 3, 5], [2, 4]) == [1, 2, 3, 4, 5])
{
  match xs { [] => ys [x, ..xs_rest] => match ys { [] => xs [y, ..ys_rest] => if (x <= y) then ([x] ++ merge_sorted(xs_rest, ys)) else ([y] ++ merge_sorted(xs, ys_rest)) } }
}

fn drop(xs: List[Int], k: Int) -> List[Int]
  requires ((k >= 0) and (k <= len(xs)))
  ensures (len(result) == (len(xs) - k))
  ensures forall x in result: contains(xs, x)
  effects pure
  example (drop([1, 2, 3], 1) == [2, 3])
  example (drop([1, 2, 3], 3) == [])
  example (drop([1, 2, 3], 0) == [1, 2, 3])
{
  if (k == 0) then xs else match xs { [] => [] [_, ..t] => drop(t, (k - 1)) }
}

fn take(xs: List[Int], k: Int) -> List[Int]
  requires ((k >= 0) and (k <= len(xs)))
  ensures (len(result) == k)
  ensures forall x in result: contains(xs, x)
  effects pure
  example (take([1, 2, 3], 1) == [1])
  example (take([1, 2, 3], 3) == [1, 2, 3])
  example (take([1, 2, 3], 0) == [])
{
  if (k == 0) then [] else match xs { [] => [] [h, ..t] => ([h] ++ take(t, (k - 1))) }
}

fn rotate_left(xs: List[Int], k: Int) -> List[Int]
  requires ((k >= 0) and (k <= len(xs)))
  ensures (len(result) == len(xs))
  ensures forall x in xs: contains(result, x)
  ensures forall x in result: contains(xs, x)
  effects pure
  example (rotate_left([1, 2, 3, 4], 1) == [2, 3, 4, 1])
  example (rotate_left([1, 2, 3, 4], 3) == [4, 1, 2, 3])
  example (rotate_left([1, 2, 3, 4], 0) == [1, 2, 3, 4])
  example (rotate_left([], 0) == [])
{
  (drop(xs, k) ++ take(xs, k))
}

fn remove_one(xs: List[Int], v: Int) -> List[Int]
  requires contains(xs, v)
  ensures (len(result) == (len(xs) - 1))
  ensures forall x in result: contains(xs, x)
  ensures forall x in xs: ((x == v) or contains(result, x))
